question: Which statement best describes The grid container?
options: display: grid turns an element into a grid container; its direct children become grid items placed into a grid you define. Like flexbox, only direct children participate. The container holds the track definitions (columns and rows) while items can span or be placed onto specific lines.

repeat() avoids writing the same track size many times. repeat(3, 1fr) equals 1fr 1fr 1fr, and repeat(12, 1fr) builds a classic 12-column grid. It also accepts auto-fit/auto-fill as the count for responsive grids and can repeat patterns like repeat(2, 100px 1fr).

These define the explicit grid by listing track sizes. grid-template-columns: 200px 1fr 200px creates three columns; grid-template-rows does the same vertically. Tracks can use px, %, fr, auto, min-content, max-content, or minmax(). Items flow into these tracks in order unless explicitly placed.

fr ('fraction') represents a share of the remaining free space in the container after fixed sizes and gaps are accounted for. grid-template-columns: 1fr 2fr makes the second column twice as wide as the first. fr is what makes grids fluid without manual percentage math, and it cleanly handles gaps.
explanation: display: grid turns an element into a grid container; its direct children become grid items placed into a grid you define. Like flexbox, only direct children participate. The container holds the track definitions (columns and rows) while items can span or be placed onto specific lines.

Grid tracks are bounded by numbered lines (starting at 1). You place an item by line with grid-column: 1 / 3 (from line 1 to line 3, spanning two columns) and grid-row similarly, or use span: grid-column: span 2. Negative line numbers count from the end, so grid-column: 1 / -1 spans the full width.

repeat(auto-fit, minmax(200px, 1fr)) creates as many columns as fit, each at least 200px and growing to fill — a responsive card grid with no media queries. auto-fill keeps empty placeholder tracks; auto-fit collapses them so existing items stretch to fill. minmax() sets a track's min and max size.
